blocks.response_text: The ESO's Table 6, based on DNO-reported data as of 13 August 2019 at 12:00, lists for UK Power Networks: Eastern 69 MW [reported], 79,390 [reported] customers, final restoration time 16:56 [reported]; London 174 MW [reported], 239,861 [reported] customers, 17:37 [reported]; Southern 69 MW [reported], 81,358 [reported] customers, 17:15 [reported].

The ESO's Table 7 gives, for UKPN SPN, 17:04 [reported] for when the ESO was informed of the demand loss and 17:13 [reported] for when it instructed restoration; for UKPN EPN, 17:04 [reported] and 17:14 [reported]; for UKPN LPN, 16:58 [reported] and 16:58 [reported]. Restoration complete is printed once across the three UKPN columns, 17:37 [reported]. The ESO's earlier answers to the E3C (data at 28 August 2019) give 17:12 [reported] for the SPN instruction, 17:14 [reported] for EPN and 'Approx. 17:40' [reported] for restoration complete.

Ofgem reports that Eastern Power Networks plc and South Eastern Power Networks plc reconnected sites without being told to do so by the ESO, and that we acknowledge we do not appear to have technically met the requirements of the Grid Code. Ofgem says these instances were caused by the configuration of our operational systems, and that the premature reconnection could potentially have jeopardised the restoration of system frequency.

As the ESO's report describes Grid Code OC6.6, after the LFDD scheme operates the DNOs must notify the ESO of its operation and are not permitted to restore automatically disconnected demand without instruction from National Grid ESO.

We confirmed to the ESO that Ipswich Hospital was not part of our LFDD protection zone and that LFDD did not affect the substations supplying it. Our time-stamped data show the hospital's load reducing by half in a period of 14 seconds [reported].

We confirmed that LFDD did not affect the Victoria line. Our control room contacted London Underground, which confirmed that it had not lost power supplies at any stations but had an internal traction issue.
